passage.text: In 1998, Malee Somboon was 25 years old and had almost no money.
passage.reading: ɪn ˌnaɪnˈtiːn ˈnaɪnti ˈeɪt, ˈmɑːliː sɑːmˈbuːn wʌz ˈtwɛnti ˈfaɪv ˈjɪrz ˈoʊld ənd ˈhæd ˈɔːlmoʊst ˈnoʊ ˈmʌni.

passage.text: She borrowed 5,000 baht from her mother and started selling boat noodles at a small stall near a busy market in Bangkok.
passage.reading: ʃiː ˈbɑːroʊd ˈfaɪv ˈθaʊzənd ˈbɑːt frəm hɜːr ˈmʌðər ənd ˈstɑːrtɪd ˈsɛlɪŋ ˈboʊt ˌnuːdəlz ət ə ˈsmɔːl ˈstɔːl ˈnɪr ə ˈbɪzi ˈmɑːrkɪt ɪn ˈbæŋkɑːk.

passage.text: She worked from five in the morning until late at night, seven days a week.
passage.reading: ʃiː ˈwɜːrkt frəm ˈfaɪv ɪn ðə ˈmɔːrnɪŋ ənˈtɪl ˈleɪt ət ˈnaɪt, ˈsɛvən ˈdeɪz ə ˈwiːk.

passage.text: Her noodles became famous by word of mouth: happy customers told their friends, and their friends told their families.
passage.reading: hɜːr ˈnuːdəlz bɪˈkeɪm ˈfeɪməs baɪ ˈwɜːrd əv ˈmaʊθ: ˈhæpi ˈkʌstəmərz ˈtoʊld ðɛr ˈfrɛndz, ənd ðɛr ˈfrɛndz ˈtoʊld ðɛr ˈfæməliz.

passage.text: Soon, people were waiting in line for an hour to eat at her little stall.
passage.reading: ˈsuːn, ˈpiːpəl wɜːr ˈweɪtɪŋ ɪn ˈlaɪn fər ən ˈaʊər tə ˈiːt ət hɜːr ˈlɪtəl ˈstɔːl.

passage.text: In 2005, she opened her first restaurant with her younger brother.
passage.reading: ɪn ˈtuː ˈθaʊzənd ˈfaɪv, ʃiː ˈoʊpənd hɜːr ˈfɜːrst ˈrɛstərɑːnt wɪð hɜːr ˈjʌŋɡər ˈbrʌðər.

passage.text: Ten years later, they had twelve restaurants in Bangkok and Chiang Mai.
passage.reading: ˈtɛn ˈjɪrz ˈleɪtər, ðeɪ ˈhæd ˈtwɛlv ˈrɛstərɑːnts ɪn ˈbæŋkɑːk ənd ˈtʃjɑːŋ ˈmaɪ.

passage.text: Today, Malee's Noodles is a chain of 40 restaurants, and it employs more than 600 people.
passage.reading: təˈdeɪ, ˈmɑːliːz ˈnuːdəlz ɪz ə ˈtʃeɪn əv ˈfɔːrti ˈrɛstərɑːnts, ənd ɪt ɪmˈplɔɪz ˈmɔːr ðən ˈsɪks ˈhʌndrəd ˈpiːpəl.

passage.text: As the founder of a big company, Malee is very busy.
passage.reading: əz ðə ˈfaʊndər əv ə ˈbɪɡ ˈkʌmpəni, ˈmɑːliː ɪz ˈvɛri ˈbɪzi.

passage.text: But every Monday, she still visits one of her restaurants and tastes the noodles herself.
passage.reading: bʌt ˈɛvri ˈmʌndeɪ, ʃiː ˈstɪl ˈvɪzɪts ˈwʌn əv hɜːr ˈrɛstərɑːnts ənd ˈteɪsts ðə ˈnuːdəlz hɜːrˈsɛlf.

passage.text: "The noodles must taste the same as they did in 1998," she says.
passage.reading: ðə ˈnuːdəlz mʌst ˈteɪst ðə ˈseɪm əz ðeɪ ˈdɪd ɪn ˌnaɪnˈtiːn ˈnaɪnti ˈeɪt, ʃiː ˈsɛz.

passage.text: What is her advice for young entrepreneurs?
passage.reading: ˈwʌt ɪz hɜːr ədˈvaɪs fər ˈjʌŋ ˌɑːntrəprəˈnɜːrz?

passage.text: "Start small, and look after every customer," she says.
passage.reading: ˈstɑːrt ˈsmɔːl, ənd ˈlʊk ˈæftər ˈɛvri ˈkʌstəmər, ʃiː ˈsɛz.

passage.text: "If your food is good, people will talk about it. That's the best advertising there is."
passage.reading: ɪf jʊr ˈfuːd ɪz ˈɡʊd, ˈpiːpəl wɪl ˈtɔːk əˈbaʊt ɪt. ðæts ðə ˈbɛst ˈædvərtaɪzɪŋ ðɛr ˈɪz.
